html:
Auschwitz was the largest Nazi German concentration and extermination camp, near Oświęcim in occupied southern Poland, where about 1.1 million people were murdered between 1940 and 1945.

It began as a camp for Polish political prisoners. From 1942 the Birkenau camp became the main site for killing Jews from across Europe in gas chambers. About one million of the dead were Jews, along with Poles, Roma and Soviet prisoners. Prisoners judged fit were forced to work, many for industrial firms, and doctors such as Josef Mengele carried out experiments. The Soviet army freed the camp on 27 January 1945. It is now a museum and memorial, and 27 January is Holocaust Remembrance Day. It is the main symbol of the Holocaust and of Nazi crimes in World War II.
sum: Auschwitz was the largest Nazi German concentration and extermination camp, near Oświęcim in occupied southern Poland, where about 1.1 million people were murdered between 1940 and 1945.
